bug_semantics: PATCH /api/users/{id}/preferences (src/API/UserController.php::updateUserPreference) iterates the JSON body and calls UserPreference::setValue() for any named preference that already exists after PrepareUserEvent, including hourly_rate and internal_rate. UserPreferenceSubscriber correctly marks those two preferences disabled (setEnabled(false)) when the target user lacks the hourly-rate permission, and the web forms hide them, but the API never consults isEnabled() and Doctrine still persists the mutated values. An authenticated user who can edit their own profile can therefore raise their billed/internal rates (CWE-915 mass assignment / BOPA), which then flow into timesheets and invoices.
flaw_origin: The unguarded preference-write loop was first authored on 2025-09-26 in d807cdeae9448dee20f3eceab76a03f1760c0b88 ('new API method to set user preferences') on PR #5621, then squash-landed on main as 7937fa281a4831737e3264f53466a7e4b4ce9768 (Release 2.40.0). The method copies the existing Activity/Customer/Project PATCH /{id}/meta pattern (lookup by name, then setValue, no enabled check) onto user preferences, where hourly_rate/internal_rate are RBAC-gated. Tests at introduction only covered happy-path mock fields and request-shape errors, not disabled financial preferences. The isEnabled() deny was added later in 870944ea0059e2024681dd39e0ead6f8848a9c73 and shipped in 2.53.0.

reasoning: CVE-2026-40486 / GHSA-qh43-xrjm-4ggp is a published, non-withdrawn mass-assignment bug: the user-preferences PATCH endpoint saved hourly_rate and internal_rate even when PrepareUserEvent had marked those preferences disabled for users without hourly-rate. The GUI already gated the fields; the new API did not. Line history on main first shows the unguarded loop in squash 7937fa28 (Release 2.40.0 / PR 5621). That squash aggregates a 20-commit release branch and is not a BIC. The public PR member d807cdea is the smallest commit that actually inserted updateUserPreference and $meta->setValue($value); its parent d7f77f69 lacks the function, the UserController blob is identical to the squash/2.40.0 blob, and later 2.42/2.45 edits do not touch the sink. The mechanism therefore originates in 2.40.0 and remains through 2.52.0 until 870944ea (landed by 999d820d / 2.53.0) adds the isEnabled() access-denied check. AI judgment is BIC-only: d807cdea is authored and committed by maintainer Kevin Papst with no commit-object AI marker, so the real vulnerability is human-authored.
